recipes.name: Roasted Peppers with Pine Nuts and Parsley
ingredients_raw: salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Preheat the oven's broiler and set the oven rack at about 6 inches from the heat source. Line a baking sheet with aluminum foil. Cut the peppers in half from top to bottom; remove the stem, seeds, and ribs, then place the peppers cut sides down onto the prepared baking sheet. Cook under the preheated broiler until the skin of the peppers has blackened and blistered, about 10 minutes. Place the blackened peppers into a bowl, and tightly seal with plastic wrap. Allow the peppers to steam as they cool, about 20 minutes. Once cool, remove the skins and discard.

Toast the pine nuts in a small dry skillet over medium-low heat, swirling the pine nuts in the skillet until they turn a light tan color and have a nutty fragrance, 1 to 2 minutes. Remove from heat and pour into a small bowl to prevent them from overcooking.

Slice the roasted peppers into strips, and arrange decoratively onto a serving platter, alternating red and yellow strips. Sprinkle the peppers with toasted pine nuts, raisins, garlic, and parsley, drizzle with olive oil, and season to taste with salt and black pepper.

raw_recipe.headline: Roasted Peppers with Pine Nuts and Parsley
raw_recipe.description: A beautiful and easy appetizer or side dish of roasted red and yellow peppers is drizzled with olive oil and sprinkled with garlic, golden raisins and toasted pine nuts.

review.reviewBody: This makes a nice side dish for roasted meat, but I think that it would also be good with pasta or bruschetta. The sweetness from the raisins adds a wonderful dimension to the taste. I used a toasted butternut squash seed oil for depth of flavor. The flavor improved after marinating overnight.

What a pleasant surprise. Some neighbors had stopped by bringing a bottle of wine, so even though I’d planned to make this over the weekend, just thought it might be good as an appetizer (it was, we all enjoyed it). I’ve roasted bell peppers on the grill, but never under the broiler, and am happy to say that the broiler works just fine. Everybody’s stove is different, but I took my peppers out at 6 minutes rather than 10, for fear they literally were going to burn up. After steaming for 20 minutes, the skins peeled easily, just as they should have. I added a few mozzarella balls and olives to the center of the plate. I really just eyeballed everything, the peppers were so sweet, the pine nuts were toasty and crunchy, and those raisins are not to be omitted, delicious. Very, very nice.
This was great! Wonderful side dish and compliments ANYTHING. I went the caper route instead of raisin. But I'm not against trying them out next round. Thanks so much for the keeper.
I was skeptical but the raisins worked well
We love this recipe! Try skipping the raisons & using capers.
Try roasting the garlic then chop and sprinkle it.
VERY tasty recipe! I made this for Christmas and the whole family loved it!
